items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10's PushReaction enum is NORMAL/DESTROY/BLOCK/IGNORE/PUSH_ONLY (javap-verified). The gameplay-facts exporter writes the vanilla name verbatim (VanillaGameplayFactsExporter.java:50). The jar census counts 1.21.10 facts as NORMAL 22,669 / DESTROY 6,847 / BLOCK 91 / PUSH_ONLY 64 states (total 29,671; method validated on 1.21.7 with 0 mismatches across 1,105 blocks). But the loader (data.rs:883-886) matches ONLY the 26.3 names (PUSH/POPPED/IMMOVEABLE/IGNORE_ENTITY) and defaults everything else to PushPull, so all 29,671 states load as PushPull: DESTROY blocks are pushed instead of popped, BLOCK blocks pushed instead of blocking, PUSH_ONLY terracotta pushed from any side. The reaction switch itself (pistons.rs:368-372) matches vanilla's map - it just never sees anything but PushPull.
items.title: Push-reaction loader matches no 1.21.10 value: every state loads as PushPull

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10's PistonBaseBlock.isPushable refuses four blocks by hardcoded name at bytecode offsets 44-85: OBSIDIAN, CRYING_OBSIDIAN, RESPAWN_ANCHOR, REINFORCED_DEEPSLATE. The port's is_pushable (pistons.rs:328-372) has no obsidian check at all - a piston pushes obsidian like stone. The named table has obsidian (:270) and respawn_anchor (:372) but no crying_obsidian or reinforced_deepslate, so even a name-based fix needs two new named entries. Obsidian's reaction is NORMAL, so this is a separate missing hardcode from B2-G02, exactly as in 1.21.7 (G9).
items.title: is_pushable lacks vanilla's hardcoded obsidian-family refusal

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10 refuses a block at y < minY || y > maxY (offsets 0-33) and refuses an UP-push only from y == maxY (offsets 106-125) - a block AT y == 320 is pushable sideways/down. The port (pistons.rs:337) computes max_y as self.level.max_y() - 1; with max_y() == 320 (mod.rs:606-608) the port's max is 319, so it refuses y == 320 outright and refuses an UP-push from 319. Off by one at the ceiling, exactly as in 1.21.7 (G10).
items.title: is_pushable Y-bound off by one at the ceiling

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10's DiodeBlock.neighborChanged has NO same-block guard - it goes straight to canSurvive at offset 0, then checkTickOnNeighbor, else dropResources + removeBlock + updateNeighborsAt in all directions (offsets 0-94). The port (redstone.rs:673-675, diode_neighbor_changed) returns early when the block at pos is no longer the diode, so a repeater/comparator that has already been replaced skips the handling vanilla would still run. The port carries the 26.2-form guard. redstone.rs is byte-identical between the 1.21.7 and 1.21.10 trees, so this defect exists in 1.21.7 too but was never minted there.
items.title: DiodeBlock.neighborChanged carries the 26.2 same-block guard vanilla 1.21.10 does not have

items.evidence: NEW in this run. crates/horizon-prepare/src/survival.rs:45 still reads ("RedstoneWireBlock", "RedstoneWire") - the 26.3 spelling. The table binds the world generator's feature-placement survival rules: bind_definitions (:102-117) looks up each block's owner class in CLASS_RULES and silently binds NO rule on miss, so redstone_wire gets no entry in survival-rules.json (the exporter carries the vanilla class RedStoneWireBlock). The file's own pattern shows the author knew this failure mode: the FarmBlock entry (:29-31) carries the comment 'without the 1.21.10 name farmland binds no survival rule' - farmland, lily pad and dry vegetation were fixed this way, but the wire was missed. The 1.21.7 tree has the same wrong line, so this is the un-minted prepare half of 1.21.7's G7: moot in 1.21.7, now the surviving half of the defect. Practical impact is small (no vanilla feature places redstone wire).
items.title: NEW: wire's prepare-side survival rule never binds - survival.rs still uses the wrong class name

systemic_note: The 1.21.10 tree IS the 1.21.11-template lineage, and it shows in exactly one place: the class-alias mechanism fixes the wire (1.21.7 G7) at runtime, plus farmland/snow/fungus/roots/path. But the alias mechanism is a table-layer fix and the deeper behaviour defects survive untouched: the push-reaction loader still matches only the 26.3 names (G8), is_pushable still lacks the obsidian hardcode (G9) and still computes the ceiling off by one (G10), and the diode guard still carries the 26.2 form (B2-G07 - a defect the 1.21.7 sweep missed entirely, since redstone.rs is byte-identical between the trees). The template fixed the dispatch layer; the logic layer still carries the 26.3 form. The 26.2 tree is the natural reference for the G8/G9/G10 repairs. Two 1.21.7 items NEVER EXISTED (G11, G12) - 1.21.7's own bytecode contradicts both premises, and the 26.x runs' 'vanilla changed' framing was wrong; the 1.21.7 ledger needs correcting (same correction class as the 26.1.2 B5-G18 bell correction). The oracle gap is a version-shape gap, not oracle rot: 26.1.2's oracles (32/4/1/cascade, three passing) look nothing like 1.21.10's (63/36/1/2/1/1/cascade) because 1.21.10 lacks the whole 26.x API surface (gamerules package, clock, blockscan, attributes, permissions, zombie subpackage, 26.3-form ctors, useNativeTransport). The E6 line needs a proper oracle-adaptation pass; the three single-break oracles (Persistence, PistonPush, PistonMovement) are the cheapest wins. NEW for 1.21.10: the wire's prepare-side survival rule never binds (B2-G08) - the runtime half of G7 was fixed, the prepare half was not; and no prepared horizon-client data exists in the worktree, so the driver runs and level::tests need a prepare run first (B2-H01/B2-H02).
